newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares fall as buyers wait for results.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares fall as buyers wait for results.

text.p: Lithuanian shares continued to stumble on Wednesday as investors waited for first quarter results, dealers said.
"The prospects this week don't look that great," said one dealer, summing up the bearish mood of market players.
External factors were mixed, with some Eastern European bourses gaining while others, including neighbouring Latvia and Slovenia, fell.
Lithuanian Gas continued its slide, falling to 1.79 litas from 1.98 litas in trade of 219,000 litas and dealers said it would probably ease some more.
Dealers said the market was responding to the state-run gas firm's recent statements concerning its 1996 results, which show a loss of at least 78 million litas.

Final results have not been released yet as the company's shareholders' meeting, originally scheduled for Monday, was postponed for two weeks because of a dispute with the auditors over legal documents.

The session's few gainers included Birzai Dairy, which rose 2.15 percent to 9.50 litas in trade of 150,500 litas and cardboard producer Medienos Plaushas, which advanced to 13.10 litas from 12.80 litas in trade of almost 21,000 litas.
Dealers said both firms looked to be a bit underpriced.
The long-term outlook for the equities market looks brighter, with a group of senior Western fund managers arriving in Vilnius Wednesday for a two-day fact finding visit.
